text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
The United States' second president JOHN ADAMS, who signed the Declaration of Independence and negotiated the end of the War of Independence, was born in 1735.
Irish-born dramatist RICHARD BRINSLEY SHERIDAN, who wrote "School for Scandal" and "The Critic", was born in 1751.
French impressionist painter ALFRED SISLEY was born in 1840.
French film director LOUIS MALLE, whose films included "The Lovers", was born in 1932.

United States songwriter EDDIE HOLLAND, who started his career as a singer, was born in 1939. He wrote hits for the 'Supremes', 'Four Tops' and MARVIN GAYE. EDDIE's only singing hit was "Jamie" (1962).

British drummer CHRIS SLADE, who started with TOM PAXTON in 1971, was born in 1946. He was with 'Manfred Mann's Earthband' from 1972 to 1978. He then played with FRANKIE MILLER, URIAH HEEP, GARY NUMAN and DENNY LAINE.
UK lead guitarist with 'Eighth Wonder' GEOFF BEAUCHAMP was born in 1962.
** EVENTS **
1485 : King HENRY VII of England established the Yeoman
of the Guard.
1905 : In the "October Manifesto", Russian Tsar NICHOLAS
II agreed to grant civil liberties and elections after coming under pressure from striking workers. The move was an attempt to avoid a revolution.
1918 : The Slovaks agreed to a union with the Czechs
under the name of Czechoslovakia.
1925 : A 15-year-old office boy WILLIAM TAYNTON became
the first person on television. He was filmed at JOHN LOGIE BAIRD's London workshop.
1934 : Italy's leader BENITO MUSSOLINI ordered all six to
eight-year-olds to undertake pre-military training. A month later teachers were ordered to wear fascist uniforms in the classroom.
1938 : The power of the airwaves was clearly demonstrated

in New York. The gripping radio dramatisation of "The War of the Worlds" by ORSON WELLS and the Mercury Players caused many listeners to believe aliens had landed. Despite several broadcast warnings by CBS that the programme was fiction thousands of New Yorkers panicked. Police switchboards were jammed, and roads and churches were packed as people tried to escape the invading Martians.
1942 : News of Australian prisoners-of-war being forced

to work on the Burma railway reached Australia. Three thousand Aussie POWS, among 15,000 captured at the fall of Singapore, had been taken to Burma to work on a Japanese rail link with Thailand. The prisoners from Changi in Malaya had been encouraged to volunteer for "light work". Most of the men were sick and were unaware of the Japanese plans for them. The "light work" was actually heavy labour clearing thick jungle undergrowth, cutting down trees, drilling rock and building bridges over fast-flowing mountain rivers.
1951 : Australian wool prices hit new heights with a
record price of 375 pence per pound. The start of the Korean War in June 1950 had increased demand for wool, needed for military uniforms.
1967 : Rolling Stone BRIAN JONES was jailed for drug
offences.
1974 : MUHAMMAD ALI knocked out GEORGE FOREMAN to regain
his title as world heavyweight boxing champion.
1979 : The inventor of the "bouncing bombs" SIR BARNES
NEVILLE WALLIS died. The British aircraft designer's invention played a key role in World War Two.
1988 : The head of the Unification Church, Rev. SUN MYUNG

MOON presided over one of the biggest mass weddings in history. In the South Korean ceremony 6516 couples, in identical wedding attire, paraded before their Moonie Master. The couples had been personally matched by the cult leader. The newly-weds then spent 40 days getting to know each other before they were allowed to consumate their marriages.
1994 : America's Secret Service officers arrested MARTIN
DURAN for firing several shots at the White House in Washington. Some of the bullets reportedly narrowly missed President BILL CLINTON's bedroom window.
1995 : Voters in Canada's Quebec province voted by a
narrow margin in a referendum to remain part of Canada.
